engagement_title: STATIC FOX channel pack: pull the strongest frame out of six mixed light captures and bring them to one loud house look, cut the mascot properly for reuse, recover the fox head emblem off the merch patch, and hand back the thumbnails, the title plate and the end card as one editable file
vertical: Music, film, publishing and media, mid tier comedy gaming channel funded by advertising and memberships (Manchester, England)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com comedy gameplay post carried in the ledger, where a creator supplies raw captures plus rough notes and their own custom graphics and asks for an entertaining fast paced upload with reaction zooms, on screen text call outs and meme cutaways, a thumbnail, and a reusable project file they can keep working in. Four of the literal asks in that post sit on the connector's not available list and are re cast honestly rather than faked: timeline trims to flagged timestamps, animated reaction zooms, motion graphic call outs composited over the picture, and meme overlays burned into the video. What survives is the part that post was actually paying for and never articulated, which is a channel front that looks like one channel: the reaction zoom becomes a punched in still crop on the thumbnail, the call out becomes a title plate the creator drops into their own editor, the meme cutaway is dropped as undeliverable and said so, and the reusable project file becomes a native editable document carrying every canvas at its own size. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the rest real: an ink level recovery off a photographed embroidered patch, a knockout that can be inspected and re routed where it bites, and mixed canvas authoring into a document the creator opens and edits themselves.
client_one_liner: My uploads do fine once people click, my grid looks like six different channels, and the fox that goes on everything only exists as a render I cannot cut out cleanly and a photo of a patch on my hoodie.
client_brief:
STATIC FOX, channel pack

I run a comedy gaming channel out of Manchester. Six uploads a month, co op disasters and bad decisions, plus a members stream on Sundays. Around four hundred thousand subscribers, income from advertising and memberships, audience mostly fifteen to twenty five.

The problem is the front of the channel. Once people click, the videos do fine. The click is where I lose. My thumbnails are whatever I threw together at two in the morning, so the grid does not look like one channel and none of them punch. I want a proper set, and more than that I want to be able to make more of them myself without asking anyone.

The captures. I have pulled six from the last few months that hold the moments I want on the thumbnails. They were recorded across two setups and my room light changed halfway through, so they do not match at all. Pull the strongest frame out of each and make the six read like they came off one channel. Loud is correct here. My audience is not looking for tasteful, and if you make this look like a documentary I will not be able to use it.

Scrap. Scrap is the fox. He was drawn for me two years ago and he goes on everything, so I need him cut out properly once and reused, not redrawn slightly differently on every thumbnail.

The patch. My merch patch has the fox head emblem embroidered on it and the original file is long gone. All I have is a photo of the patch on my hoodie. I need that emblem back as artwork I can actually put on things.

The shorts. One short vertical cut per capture for the feeds, with my commentary cleaned up. Nothing stretched and nothing blown up to fit.

And I want the thumbnails, a title plate for the shorts and an end card in one file I can open and change myself, because my titles change constantly and I am not paying for a new file every time.

Plus a note on what you did and what I can and cannot do with the fox.
price_band_and_audience: Mid tier comedy gaming channel, advertising and membership income, audience fifteen to twenty five. The band is load bearing in the opposite direction from most commissions. At this genre and this audience the work has to be loud: saturated, high contrast, faces large in frame, type heavy and unembarrassed, because that is what wins the click in a crowded feed. A restrained, tasteful, low saturation treatment with generous white space is a correct looking wrong answer that signals the wrong channel entirely and suppresses the only metric the creator is paying to move. Push the other way past loud into pure noise, with every element outlined, arrowed, glowing and shouting at once, and the grid stops reading as one channel at all, which is the exact problem the creator hired someone to fix. The judgement is loud AND coherent, and an agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even where every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Co op disasters and bad decisions.
brand_identity.sector: Mid tier comedy gaming YouTube channel: co op gameplay, reaction humour and a weekly members stream.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Running since 2019 out of Manchester, England. One creator with a home setup, six uploads a month plus a Sunday members stream.
brand_identity.about: STATIC FOX is a loud, fast comedy gaming channel built on co op chaos and the creator's on camera reactions. Around four hundred thousand subscribers watch for the disasters, the bad calls and the running jokes. The videos land once people click, so the whole brand fight happens on the thumbnail, in the feed, at a glance.
brand_identity.audience: Mostly fifteen to twenty five, watching in a crowded feed on phones. They want energy and payoff, not taste. Income comes from advertising and channel memberships.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid tier creator funded by ad revenue and memberships. The work has to be loud, saturated and heavy on the face and the moment, because that is what wins the click at this level. Restrained and tasteful reads as the wrong channel; pure noise stops reading as one channel at all. Loud and coherent is the line.
brand_identity.typography: A heavy condensed display face for titles that has to punch at thumbnail scale and survive both very short and very long titles, paired with a bold grotesque for supporting lines. Big, tight, unembarrassed. No delicate or editorial type anywhere.
brand_identity.voice: Fast, funny, self deprecating and a bit chaotic, always in on the joke. Example line the brand would write: "We had one job. We did not do the job. New one up now."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mascot, Scrap the fox in a headset, was drawn two years ago and survives only as a flat shaded render on a dark panel, with no clean cutout. The merch fox head emblem's original file is long gone and exists only as a photo of the embroidered patch on the creator's hoodie. There is no brand kit; titles and catchphrases live in a text file.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability and independence. The creator wants a set that looks like one channel and a file they can keep editing themselves, so they never have to pay for a new one when a title changes.

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_captures/ (six gameplay captures)
assets_supplied.kind: Screen captures from the last few months, each holding the moment the creator wants on a thumbnail, recorded across two setups.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Six captures, the moments are all in there. My room light changed halfway through so they will not match."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six came off the older setup at a materially smaller frame size than the rest, although every filename follows the same pattern and nothing in the folder distinguishes them, so the punched in crop the genre demands cannot be reached on those two without enlarging. A third carries the creator's own facecam window burned into the lower right of the recording itself, so the moment on that capture cannot be cropped clean of it and the crop has to be re thought rather than tightened.

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_scrap_render.png
assets_supplied.kind: The channel mascot, a fox in a headset, drawn two years ago and supplied as a flat shaded render sitting on a dark gradient panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Scrap. He goes on everything. This is the only file I have of him."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Scrap is outlined in a deep navy that sits close in value to the dark panel he was rendered on, so the one call knockout hands back a complete looking cutout that has quietly bitten the tail tip and one ear. It reads as correct at preview scale and only shows at full resolution against a light ground. The render also carries a soft glow baked into its own pixels, which comes away as a grey fringe wherever the cutout lands on anything pale.

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_patch.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the channel's merch patch, a fox head emblem embroidered in three thread colours, worn on the creator's hoodie.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The emblem off my merch. The original file is long gone."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The emblem has enclosed shapes inside it, so background removal returns a solid opaque badge rather than a knockout, and the badge looks entirely convincing until it lands on a coloured ground. The embroidery's thread texture also turns a colour accurate trace into hundreds of near identical fills that will not reproduce as a mark at any size. The patch is photographed on folded fabric, so the emblem is neither flat nor square to the camera.

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_titles.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the six upload titles, the creator's recurring catchphrases, the members call to action and the end card copy.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Titles and the lines I always use. The members line has to be on the end card."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six titles run more than twice the length of the others, so a single type size and a single measure cannot serve the set and the shortest titles will look underset wherever the longest one fits.

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_refs.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of three channel grids the creator admires, supplied as a direction reference rather than as a spec.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the energy I want. Not the exact style, the energy."

acceptance_bar: The six graded frames read as ONE channel when they are laid out the way a channel grid lays them: one contrast, one saturation discipline, one sense of how large the moment sits in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.

The set is loud and coherent at the same time. A tasteful, low saturation, generously spaced grid fails this commission even if every technical gate passes, and so does a grid where every element is outlined, glowing and shouting until nothing reads.

No delivered thumbnail, frame or vertical cut exceeds the pixel dimensions of the capture or frame it came from, and no returned resize report carries an enlargement entry. Reaching the thumbnail size by interpolation fails even where it looks acceptable at a glance.
Where a capture cannot carry the punch in the set needs, the crop is re thought and the reason is named in writing. Enlarging to close the gap is not an answer.

Scrap is cut once and reused identically everywhere. The cut edge holds at full resolution against the pale band as well as against the dark one, with no bitten tail, no clipped ear and no grey fringe.

The fox head emblem comes back as placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as the emblem at the size it actually sits on the end card and on a coloured ground.
The vertical cuts are shorter than their sources, carry cleaned commentary, and are reframed by reduction only. Cleaning after cutting is not the same job and does not count.

All the canvases arrive in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, with the titles as text that can be retyped, the emblem as real vector shapes, and every picture carried inside the file rather than pointed at. The self contained source it was built from comes with it.
The type system holds the two long titles and the four short ones without one of them looking underset, and it survives the handover on every canvas rather than only the first one.
One type system across every canvas, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.

The note states per frame what was applied and why that capture differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, which captures could not carry the punch in and what was done instead, and what can and cannot be done with the fox.

adobe_surfaces.role: Reads what each capture actually is before any crop or delivery size is promised, because the filenames are uniform and the recordings are not. Pulls the strongest frame out of each of the six, cleans the commentary before anything is cut so the cleaning applies to the whole take rather than to the fragments that survived, produces the short vertical pieces by the engagement route rather than by timestamps, and reframes to vertical by reduction only.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_preset, image_apply_monochromatic_tint, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It sets the house look on the strongest frame and brings the other five to it off each frame's own neutral rather than through one batched curve, cuts the punched in reaction crops without enlarging anything, knocks the mascot out once and inspects the edge where his outline and his rendered panel share value, and recovers the emblem at ink level off a photographed embroidered patch with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The six thumbnails, the vertical title plate and the end card as one native editable document carrying roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only thing that answers the creator's actual ask, which is to make more of these without asking anyone. Every picture must be carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the emblem goes in as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels as an uploaded file because six inlined frames pass the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system across every canvas, and the thing that has to hold two titles more than twice the length of the other four. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land loud without becoming illegible at thumbnail scale. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, every name has to be laundered into canonical form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS has to use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one thing the creator does not have, a genuine camera scale grit surface for the band the titles sit on, IP clean, with generative candidates excluded, then grades it into the same house look so it does not read as bought. The Boards half persists the shortlist the creator and their manager sign off from, placed within the per call placement cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The frames, the cutout and the emblem are raster and vector work; the thumbnails, plate and end card must be an authored fixed canvas document because the creator's stated ask is to keep editing them. The brief pins the destination, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because six captures with a uniform naming pattern are the easiest thing in this job to confuse.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read what each of the six captures actually is: frame size, duration and audio state, before any crop or delivery size is promised.
trajectory.judgement: The filenames are uniform and the recordings are not. Everything downstream, the punch in, the thumbnail size and the vertical height, is bounded by what each file turns out to be.
trajectory.produces: A per capture note of true dimensions, duration and audio condition.

trajectory.action: Pull the strongest frame out of each of the six captures.
trajectory.judgement: Strongest means the moment the creator described, with the reaction legible, rather than the cleanest looking frame. A tidy frame with nothing happening in it is worthless on this channel.
trajectory.produces: Six candidate frames, one per capture, at each capture's own scale.

trajectory.action: Preview all six frames and triage them: where each frame's neutral sits, which setup each belongs to, how much clean room surrounds the moment, and what is already burned into the recording.
trajectory.judgement: Two setups and a light change mean at least two correction families, and the amount of room around the moment decides per frame whether the punch in the genre wants is even available before any crop is attempted.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering neutral, setup, available room and anything burned into the picture.

trajectory.action: Author two candidate house looks on the strongest single frame, one at maximum saturation and contrast and one held slightly back, and pick one with a written justification against the genre and the audience.
trajectory.judgement: This is the taste decision the whole commission turns on. Loud is correct here and restraint is the failure mode, but past a point loud stops reading as one channel and starts reading as noise. The pick has to be argued, not asserted.
trajectory.produces: Two treatments on one frame and a written pick with the reasoning.

trajectory.action: Bring all six frames to the chosen look with their own calls, off each frame's own neutral, recording the parameters applied to each.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a grid of six, not six good frames. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong across two setups and a light change, so the destination is held constant and reached by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Six frames on one house look with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the punched in reaction crops at the thumbnail spec, reading what each crop reports about what it actually did to the pixels rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The genre wants the face large and the moment tight, and how far that can go is a property of each capture rather than a style choice. Where the punch cannot be reached honestly, the composition changes rather than the pixel count.
trajectory.produces: Six thumbnail base crops with every returned resize report recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Knock the mascot out once for reuse, then inspect the edge at full resolution against both a pale and a dark ground rather than at preview scale.
trajectory.judgement: Preview scale is where a bitten edge hides. A cutout that will sit on every thumbnail has to be correct at the edge before it is reused, because a fault carried into eight canvases is eight faults.
trajectory.produces: One reusable mascot cutout, edge inspected on both grounds.

trajectory.action: Recover the fox head emblem off the patch: an ink level selection naming the emblem's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the stitched emblem rather than the hoodie, which polarity to trace, and that the binary plate is what traces into a mark while a colour accurate plate turns thread texture into hundreds of fills. Background removal on an emblem with enclosed shapes returns a solid badge.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent emblem plus a note on what its enclosed shapes required.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the grit surface the title band sits on, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it into the house look.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the surface whose existing contrast can be brought to the chosen look rather than the best looking thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale surface graded into the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a fifteen to twenty five audience in a crowded feed, and it has to survive two titles more than twice the length of the other four without either extreme looking wrong.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the six thumbnail canvases, the vertical title plate and the end card, each root declaring its own canvas size, every picture inlined as image data, the mascot and the emblem placed inside explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, and family and weight declared on every text element. Upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A picture left as a reference is not a picture, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas edge, and a global canvas override is precisely what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is holding the loud direction across eight canvases so the grid reads as one channel.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole channel pack, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at a pack of eight.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the other seven.

trajectory.action: Clean the commentary on each capture, then produce the short vertical piece from the cleaned take, then reframe to vertical by reduction only.
trajectory.judgement: Cleaning has to precede cutting or it only touches whatever fragments survived. The shortening route works from engagement rather than from timestamps, so the ask is a short cut rather than a re edit, and the vertical height is bounded by each source rather than by the platform.
trajectory.produces: Six short vertical cuts with cleaned commentary, each at or below its source dimensions.

trajectory.action: Create the shortlist board and add the graded frames, the cutout and the licensed surface within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is not a success, and the vector emblem is not boardable, so it belongs in the note rather than being silently absent from the board.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per frame and why each capture differs, the treatment pick and its reasoning, the type system by role, every resize any tool reported, which captures could not carry the punch in and what was done instead, and what can and cannot be done with the fox.
trajectory.judgement: The note is what lets the creator make the next six themselves, which is the actual ask. It has to be honest about the two captures that could not be punched in and about the emblem's enclosed shapes.
trajectory.produces: A written handover note covering the run, the gaps and the limitations.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the punched in crop this genre requires can be reached honestly on each of these six captures. How far in the crop can go depends on where the moment actually sits inside each recording and on what each recording actually is, and the two are independent: a frame with the reaction in the corner needs a harder punch than one with it centred. The crop tool answers a request that lands under the delivery size by interpolating up to a hard ceiling and returning a plausible, correctly sized, apparently sharp file, reporting what it did solely as an entry inside its own returned tradeoff record with an enlargement factor. There is no warning, no error and no refusal, and the softness is not visible at the scale a response is inspected at.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the punch in is a per frame decision that can only be made after the frame is pulled and looked at, and no parameter refuses to enlarge. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the moments the creator wants and says nothing stretched or blown up to fit, which is a standing preference rather than a disclosure that a tool quietly enlarges and says so only in a field nobody reads. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different composition on the affected captures, a wider frame with the thumbnail built around it, rather than the same crop attempted again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the returned tradeoff record on every crop, re compose the thumbnails for the captures that cannot carry the punch honestly, and re judge the whole grid for coherence once two of six are framed wider than the rest.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A six thumbnail grid in which two are visibly soft in the feed at the exact size the click is decided, on a channel whose only paid objective is the click, delivered against a run in which every call reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Where the mascot's knockout actually bites. Scrap is outlined in a deep navy and was rendered on a dark gradient panel, so along the tail tip and one ear the subject and the ground carry close to the same value and subject detection has no edge to find there. The returned cutout is complete looking, correctly shaped and entirely convincing at preview scale and against a dark ground, and the loss only appears at full resolution against a pale one. The soft glow baked into the render's own pixels behaves the same way, arriving as a grey fringe that is invisible until the cutout lands on something light. Which parts of this particular drawing on this particular panel fail is not predictable from looking at the render.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it. Inspecting at full resolution on both grounds is the discipline that catches it, and it is a discipline an agent adopts because it has been burned, not because a response said anything. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the fox goes on everything and must be cut properly once, which is the client's requirement rather than a warning about where the edge fails. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the fix is a different chain, a named material selection inverted and filled to isolate the region the detector could not see, rather than the same knockout call repeated.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cut the failing regions through an explicit selection of the mascot's own outline colour, inverted and filled, re inspect at full resolution on both a pale and a dark ground, and only then propagate the corrected cutout across every canvas that had already been laid out with the first version.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eight canvases carrying the same fox with a bitten tail and a grey halo, on the one element the creator explicitly said must be identical everywhere, discovered by the audience rather than by anyone in the engagement.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the loud treatment the whole pack is built on. Authored the natural way, the neon wash over each frame is a blend mode, the glow behind the mascot is a blur or a layered shadow, and the title has an outline so it survives whatever is behind it. This importer drops a blend mode to a plain opaque shape, drops a blur outright, truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, drops an outline entirely, and renders stroked type with a transparent fill completely invisible. Every one of those returns success with no warning. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition shows the first artboard only, so seven of the eight canvases can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) The drop happens at import, which is the last step, so no ordering precedes it, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable loud constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for loud and the acceptance line about loud and coherent is the client's art direction rather than a warning about normalisation. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is to move the effect upstream into the raster the canvas carries, or to rebuild the treatment out of constructions the importer keeps, and then to re judge whether the grid still reads as one channel.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the treatment out of surviving constructions or bake the wash and the glow into the upstream frames, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit all eight canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A pack handed over in which the neon wash is an opaque slab covering the moment, the mascot sits on a flat rectangle instead of a glow and the titles are invisible, on the seven canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: STATIC FOX house frames, six captures
deliverables.spec: Six frames, one pulled from each capture, brought to one house look with one contrast and one saturation discipline across two setups and a light change, each at or below its own capture's dimensions, with a per frame parameter log and a written record of the two candidate treatments and why the chosen one wins in this genre. One set with one look, not one frame at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Scrap cutout for reuse
deliverables.spec: One mascot cutout carrying genuine alpha, cut once and reused identically on every canvas, with an edge that holds at full resolution against both a pale and a dark ground: no bitten tail, no clipped ear and no grey fringe from the glow baked into the source render. Delivered with a note of which regions needed a different route and why.

deliverables.name: Recovered fox head emblem
deliverables.spec: The merch emblem recovered from a photograph of an embroidered patch as placeable scalable vector geometry on a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, its enclosed shapes genuinely open rather than filled with hoodie, and it still reads as the emblem at the size it sits on the end card and on a coloured ground.

deliverables.name: Six vertical short cuts with cleaned commentary
deliverables.spec: One short vertical piece per capture, each shorter than its source, each carrying commentary cleaned before anything was cut rather than after, and each reframed to vertical by reduction only with no dimension exceeding its source. Delivered with the submitted parameters recorded per cut, including the source frame size that bounded it.

deliverables.name: Channel pack canvases as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying the six thumbnails, the vertical title plate and the end card as roots at their own canvas sizes, with live editable text in one licensed type system that holds both the long and the short titles, the emblem as real vector shapes, the mascot placed identically throughout, and every picture carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source it was built from, which is the durable half and the thing that answers the creator's ask to make more of these themselves.

deliverables.name: Handover note and shortlist board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per frame what was applied and why that capture differs, the treatment pick and its reasoning, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported and the file it applied to, which captures could not carry the punch in and what was done instead, the vertical cut parameters, and what can and cannot be done with the fox. Which frame in each capture is the moment, as against which frame is merely the cleanest.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns six loud gaming thumbnails. IDENTITY: these are this creator's own captured moments from their own uploads, this creator's own face and room, this creator's mascot drawn for them two years ago, and this creator's merch emblem, which has to be RECOVERED off a photographed patch rather than reinvented, because a regenerated fox is a different channel's mascot and a regenerated moment is not from the video the thumbnail promises. SPEC: six thumbnails at a delivery size that must be reached without interpolation from captures of two different sizes, plus vertical cuts shorter than their sources, is not something a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the pack is defined by being editable, because titles change constantly and the creator explicitly refuses to pay for a new file each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this crop get enlarged, did this knockout bite the tail, did the wash survive the handover, is this cut shorter than what it came from.
doability_proof: Five honestly counted surfaces, no banned capability, and every synchronous link verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, apply_preset, monochromatic_tint, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection confidence and upscale factor, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless. The three checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: crop_and_resize DOES enlarge, up to a hard two times cap, reporting it solely as an upscale factor and an entry inside its own tradeoffs array; subject knockout has no edge to find where subject and ground share value and returns a complete looking cutout anyway, while alpha itself survives crops at png output; and the importer drops blend mode, drops blur, drops outline, truncates a layered shadow to layer one and renders stroked type with a transparent fill fully invisible, all at HTTP success. VECTOR: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, remove_background returning a solid disc on enclosed interiors, the missing viewBox and the opaque path at index zero are all live findings, and colour plates trace into dozens of near identical fills while binary plates trace into a mark, which is exactly the choice the emblem forces. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline vector becomes native editable shapes, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition is documented as first artboard only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because six inlined frames pass the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, including the non standard numeric weights that make font_styles mandatory. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed because it always returns zero, licensing returned a genuine camera scale JPEG, and boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call where a 201 means partial. VIDEO AND AUDIO: video_metadata, video_render_frame, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut and video_resize are submissions whose artifacts resolve through the host's progress widget rather than synchronously in the tool result, so NO checkpoint and NO automatic gate in this task depends on a video artifact being retrievable inside the run. The video gates are properties of the submitted work: cleaning precedes cutting, the cut is a shortening rather than a timestamp trim, and the reframe never exceeds the source dimensions. AVOIDED: no vector render or vector merge, no motion graphics or compositing over video, no meme overlay burn in, no upscaling, no format conversion, no OCR, no text to image, no picture reaching Express as a reference, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above twenty.
